The finite verb names the act, the active participle raakiE- names its doer/state, and the fuEEal noun rukkaE names its performers collectively; all three shapes resolve to one nucleus.

internal_discovery.candidate_root_contribution: rkE denotes the visible, enacted bodily act/posture of bowing (bending/lowering the torso) performed as reverent submission before God, held categorically distinct from and lesser than full prostration (sjd), with which it is characteristically co-listed as a separate item. The finite verb names the act, the active participle raakiE- names its doer/state, and the fuEEal noun rukkaE names its performers collectively; all three shapes resolve to one nucleus.
internal_discovery.plain_explanation: Across all 13 occurrences the root means 'to bow' as a devotional posture. The decisive Quran-internal signal is that bowing is repeatedly listed side-by-side with prostration (sjd) as a separate act (22:26, 2:125, 22:77, 3:43, 48:29, 9:112), so the two cannot be the same act and rkE is not prostration. It is also shown to be something seen and done ('you see them bowing', 48:29) and physically fallen into (38:24), not a purely inner attitude. The account is graded MODERATE rather than STRONG because the narrow 'posture-not-abstract-submission' claim cannot be adversarially cleaned (the root has no secular/neutral bending occurrence anywhere in the corpus), and 38:24 (fell down bowing and turned in repentance) materially pulls toward either attitude/contrition or prostration-type collapse.
internal_discovery.layer_separation_note: rkE does NOT entail: (1) prostration/sjd -- always enumerated as a distinct act beside it; (2) generic worship/Eibaada -- 22:77 lists irkaEuu, usjuduu, uEbuduu as three distinct imperatives; (3) the institution of prayer/salaat as a whole -- 2:43 sets 'establish the prayer' beside 'bow with those who bow', 5:55 sets 'they establish prayer' beside 'while they bow'; (4) repentance/qunuut -- 38:24 conjoins raakiEan with a separate anaaba, 3:43 keeps uqnutii and usjudii distinct from irkaEii. No secular/mechanical 'bend' sense is attested.
internal_discovery.strongest_counterexample: 38:24:31:1 'wa-kharra raakiEan wa-anaaba' (David fell down bowing and turned in repentance). This is the single materially resistant occurrence: it is the only individual, spontaneous, non-communal, non-liturgical token; the collocate kharra ('fell/collapsed down') connotes going all the way down, which fits the deeper posture (prostration) against which rkE is elsewhere the lesser bend, straining the rkE-not-sjd contrast; and the framing by anaaba (contrite turning) rather than salaat/sjd pulls raakiEan toward attitude ('in humbled abasement') rather than the defined ritual bend. Neither resolution -- loosening posture to attitude, or letting rkE cover collapse -- is Quran-internally excluded, so 38:24 caps the grade.
internal_discovery.strongest_competitor: That rkE = 'self-humbling / reverent submission before God', with bowing merely its prototypical expression. It fits all 13 (postural cases as its literal core; 5:55 and the epithet-lists 9:112 as its attitudinal core; 77:48 refusal-to-bow as refusal-to-submit; 38:24 as self-abasement). It cannot be internally refuted because the root has zero secular/neutral occurrences to separate posture from attitude. It is nonetheless outranked as the nucleus because a pure-submission sense makes rkE redundant everywhere it is co-listed as a separate item beside sjd (22:77 even lists three with Eibaada), which the text never treats them as; the narrower postural reading is both more distinctive and better anchored (tarahum rukkaEan, 48:29). The contract's warning against a vague abstraction that fits everything applies to the competitor.

internal_discovery.rationale: All three lenses converge on one bridged nucleus -- reverent bowing, distinct from prostration -- spanning verb, participle, and fuEEal noun, Meccan and Medinan, 13/13 with no unbridged sub-class; this is a genuine derivational family, not multi-class, so UNRESOLVED is unwarranted. The postural-distinct-from-sjd core is adversarially hard to dislodge (the recurrent co-listing forces it). However STRONG is declined: (a) the sharpest useful claim -- physical posture, not abstract submission -- is not adversarially clean, because no secular bending occurrence exists to test whether reverence is a root entailment or merely the exclusive frame of use; (b) 38:24 is materially resistant (kharra + anaaba). Per the contract, material resistance caps strength at MODERATE and scope at REPRESENTATIVE. Two of three lenses (including the adversary) held MODERATE/REPRESENTATIVE; Lens B's STRONG/GENERAL is not adopted because it treats 38:24 as fully bridgeable and treats the devotional entailment as robust despite conceding it cannot be isolated adversarially.

clusters.candidate_semantic_interpretation: The finite act of bowing, commanded or (when negated) refused: irkaEuu / irkaEii 'bow!' and yarkaEuun 'they bow'. Bowing is an orderable, performable, communal act.
clusters.classification_rationale: 22:77 'irkaEuu wa-sjuduu wa-Ebuduu rabbakum' lists bowing as one distinct act alongside prostration and worship; 2:43 'wa-rkaEuu maEa r-raakiEiin' commands it jointly with a body of doers; 3:43 commands it to Mary; 77:48 'idhaa qiila lahum irkaEuu laa yarkaEuun' makes bowing-on-command the emblematic test refused by the arrogant, requiring rkE to carry its own distinct postural content.
clusters.supporting_evidence_note: All five are devotional-frame commands/negation; none carries a secular 'bend' sense. The order rkE->sjd (22:77) vs sjd->rkE (3:43) shows the pair is a devotional merism, not a fixed physical sequence.

clusters.classification_rationale: This class carries the strongest distinctiveness evidence: 48:29 'taraahum rukkaEan sujjadan' governs rkE by taraa ('you SEE them'), an observable bodily state, and the co-listing with sujuud in all three forces rkE to be a distinct, lesser posture, not prostration and not generic worship.

resistant_deep_analysis.preliminary_note: Morphologically an unambiguous raakiE- participle in the bowing family; on Lens B read as bridgeable within 'humble bodily submission before God' (kharra = physical falling, anaaba added not entailed).
resistant_deep_analysis.reconciliation_rationale: Lenses A and C (adversary) show kharra pulls toward full descent (prostration register) and anaaba pulls toward contrition/attitude, and neither is internally excluded. Under the contract, this is material resistance; it is recorded as a RESISTANT_SEAM hard case and caps the aggregate at MODERATE/REPRESENTATIVE rather than STRONG/GENERAL.

independent_verification: Three independent lenses (A, B, adversary C) each read all 13 occurrences; two of three (A, C) independently converged on MODERATE/REPRESENTATIVE with 38:24 as the resistant seam, and all three agreed the competitor 'submission' account cannot be internally refuted.
candidate_root_contribution: rkE denotes the visible, enacted bodily act/posture of bowing (bending/lowering the torso) performed as reverent submission before God, held categorically distinct from and lesser than full prostration (sjd), with which it is characteristically co-listed as a separate item. The finite verb names the act, the active participle raakiE- names its doer/state, and the fuEEal noun rukkaE names its performers collectively; all three shapes resolve to one nucleus.

layer_attribution.occurrence_evidence: 13/13 occurrences read from packet verse_text and QAC morphology: 5 finite verbs (all Form I, qac_verb_form null), 5 active participles raakiE-, 3 fuEEal nouns rukkaE. Decisive surfaces: taraahum rukkaEan sujjadan (48:29), wa-kharra raakiEan (38:24), irkaEuu wa-sjuduu wa-Ebuduu (22:77), idhaa qiila lahum irkaEuu laa yarkaEuun (77:48).
layer_attribution.derivation: One derivational family: base Form-I verb 'to bow', its active participle (doer/state), and the fuEEal intensive/collective (the bowers as a body). All shapes resolve to the single act; no derived verb forms present and none needed to bridge.
layer_attribution.lexical_class: No lexicalized non-bowing sense exists; the epithet/class uses ('the bowers', 5:55, 9:112, 22:26, 2:125) are metonymic person-for-act extensions, semantically continuous, not an independent lexical class.
layer_attribution.contextual_relation: Every token sits in a devotional frame and rkE is repeatedly co-listed with sjd, salaat, zakaat, and Eibaada. This context establishes the devotional framing and the rkE/sjd distinction, but the devotional-submission ENTAILMENT is a contextual regularity that must NOT be promoted to the root claim, since it cannot be adversarially separated from the posture; the root claim stays 'the bowing posture', with reverent submission as its exclusive frame of use.
layer_attribution.reconciliation: Divergence on 38:24 (Lens B: bridgeable/STRONG; Lenses A, C: materially resistant/MODERATE) was reconciled toward RESISTANT for that occurrence and MODERATE/REPRESENTATIVE overall, honoring the contract's material-resistance cap and the majority of independent lenses.
layer_attribution.unresolved_resistance: 38:24 persists as a materially resistant seam: raakiEan there admits either an attitude/abasement reading or a prostration-type-collapse reading, neither Quran-internally excluded. This residual, plus the untestability of posture-vs-submission (no secular occurrence), is the standing reason STRONG/UNIVERSAL is withheld.

hard_cases.reason: The one occurrence that resists the narrowest posture account and caps the grade.

evidence_basis.statement: 'wa-kharra raakiEan wa-anaaba': kharra ('fell/collapsed down') connotes full descent (the prostration register against which rkE is elsewhere the lesser bend), and the framing by anaaba (contrite turning) pulls raakiEan toward attitude/abasement rather than the defined ritual bend; neither resolution is Quran-internally excluded.

hard_cases.reason: Shows the participle can detach from the instantaneous posture into a characterizing-class reading, marking the limit of the physical-snapshot claim.

evidence_basis.statement: Read as an instantaneous snapshot, 'giving zakat while bowing' is incoherent (one does not hand out charity mid-bow); this forces the participle into its nominal characterizing sense 'of the bowing kind', showing it can float free of the momentary posture.

hard_case_representation.rationale: Both hard cases are derived from Quran-internal collocation/coherence evidence in the packet, not from external lexica. 38:24 is a genuine RESISTANT_SEAM (final RESISTANT, in counterevidence_refs); 5:55 is an ADVERSARIAL_BOUNDARY that remains CONSISTENT via metonymic nominalization. Their evidence_basis statements are echoed in strongest_counterexample and the 5:55 occurrence override note respectively.

rejection_condition.challenging_finding: A Quranic occurrence of rkE in which bowing is NOT held distinct from prostration -- i.e. rkE and sjd used interchangeably for the same act, or rkE plainly denoting full face-to-ground prostration -- or, conversely, a secular/neutral occurrence of rkE meaning merely 'bend the body' outside any reverential/devotional frame.
rejection_condition.search_location: The co-listing occurrences (22:26, 2:125, 22:77, 3:43, 48:29, 9:112) for any collapse of the rkE/sjd distinction; 38:24 for whether raakiEan functions as prostration or as attitude; the full 13 for any non-devotional bend.
rejection_condition.verification_method: Re-read each cited verse_text for whether rkE and sjd are enumerated as two items vs. equated; check whether any rkE token lacks a devotional/submissive frame; test whether the postural reading (bend torso, seen, fallen-into) fits better than the abstract-submission reading token by token.
rejection_condition.confounder_control: Do not treat shared devotional context as proof that rkE MEANS 'submission'; do not treat morphological relatedness (V / participle / fuEEal) as evidence of a single meaning without the co-listing test; exclude external lexica, tafsir, and inherited glosses; distinguish metonymic 'the bowers' (person-for-act) from a genuinely new sense.
rejection_condition.failure_consequence: If rkE were shown interchangeable with sjd, the core rkE-not-prostration boundary and the whole postural nucleus collapse (root -> REJECTED or re-scoped). If a secular bend were attested, the devotional framing would be demoted from robust-generalization to context-only, and the competitor's abstraction would gain, but the postural core would survive re-scoped.

reopen_conditions: If a segment-level Arabic alignment or additional attested occurrence shows rkE and sjd used interchangeably for the same act (breaking the rkE/sjd co-listing distinction that anchors the nucleus at 22:26, 2:125, 22:77, 3:43, 48:29, 9:112).

If any rkE occurrence is found in a secular/non-devotional frame ('bend' without reverence), which would let the posture-vs-submission question finally be tested and could re-scope the devotional entailment.

If 38:24 (wa-kharra raakiEan wa-anaaba) is re-analyzed such that raakiEan is best read as prostration-type collapse or as pure contrite attitude, which would either fracture the rkE/sjd boundary or promote the abstract-submission competitor.

falsification_evidence.status_rationale: The postural-distinct-from-prostration nucleus survives adversarial pressure across all three morphological clusters and is distinctive (the recurrent co-listing with sjd forces it). It is not marked PASSED because the sharper claim (posture, not abstract submission) cannot be adversarially isolated -- the corpus contains no secular/neutral bending occurrence -- and 38:24 remains materially resistant. Per contract, with the core holding but one occurrence resisting, the status is NOT_RUN with the resistant occurrence recorded, not PASSED or FAILED.
